notes:
Verification trail. (a) The validator: packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/inputs/update-location.input.ts:58-102 resolves location.type through classTypeMap, plainToInstance's it into UpdateBookingInputAttendeePhoneLocation_2024_08_13 (line 31, which extends the base class unchanged) and runs class-validator; the base class at packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/inputs/location.input.ts:111-119 decorates phone with @IsPhoneNumber(). class-validator 0.14.3 delegates that to libphonenumber-js 1.12.38 (yarn.lock:28692; the repo's .yarn/patches/libphonenumber-js+1.12.38.patch only unsets the CommonJS default export, it does not touch metadata). (b) The number: running libphonenumber-js against the four values, +19876543210 -> isValid() false, country undefined; +441234567890 -> true GB; +37120993151 -> true LV; +12125551234 -> true US. So the rejection is correct, not a validator bug: 987 is not an assigned NANP area code. (c) The code path works: cal.diy's own e2e test apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/e2e/update-booking-location.e2e-spec.ts:332-359 ("can update location to type attendeePhone") posts +37120993151 and asserts 200 with data.location equal to the phone; booking-location.service.ts:178 returns loc.phone for attendeePhone. The scenario would almost certainly have passed with a real number.

Fix for the scenario: replace +19876543210 with the documented example +37120993151 (or any valid E.164 number). Note the same scenario's later organizer-phone step already uses +441234567890, which IS valid, so only step 5 is affected.

Secondary, worth reporting to the doc author even though it does not change the verdict: the published OpenAPI under-specifies phone. Both UpdateBookingInputAttendeePhoneLocation_2024_08_13.phone and UpdateBookingInputPhoneLocation_2024_08_13.phone render as bare `type: string` with an example and no `format` or `pattern`, because @IsPhoneNumber() is a class-validator decorator that @nestjs/swagger does not reflect into the schema (@DocsProperty supplies only the example). A client generating a strict client from the spec has no way to know an E.164-valid number is required, and the endpoint description says nothing about it either. Adding `format: phone` / a pattern, or a sentence to the description, would close the gap. That is a docs-generation issue in cal.diy's decorators (which feed cal.com/docs api-reference/v2/openapi.json), not a behavior bug.

Not an edition mismatch: the scenario uses cal-api-version 2024-08-13, which the tested tree does support (packages/platform/constants/api.ts tops out at 2024-09-04), and steps 1-4 got real 200/201 responses, so systemic cause 1 in the brief does not apply here.

Environment noise that is NOT the cause: server.stderr.txt is full of `connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:1025` from the mail transport (no SMTP sink in the sandbox, including for the "Location Changed" notification the docs mention). Those are logged and swallowed; the successful steps 2-4 returned 200 despite them, and step 5 failed at input validation 13 ms in, before any mail was attempted.

Blame for the validation, informational only since it is not a defect: packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/inputs/location.input.ts:116 @IsPhoneNumber() traces to a31242cdc53cf1a45c9e83fb54317c6d461e486a, 2025-03-12, "refactor: v2 booking locations (#19613)" by Lauris Skraucis. The update-location input file was last touched by 089a39f59f39, 2026-03-17, "feat: add integration options for API v2 update booking location endpoint (#26363)".
